problems.title: An isosceles trapezoid and a golden ratio
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has a leg equal to its smaller base and a diagonal equal to its larger base. Find its acute angle.
problems.idea: Express the height using both the leg and the diagonal.
formulas: Let smaller base and leg be b, larger base B, height h. h²=b²−(B−b)²/4; B²=h²+(B+b)²/4.
steps: Subtracting gives B²=Bb+b². Thus B/b=(1+√5)/2.
The acute angle θ satisfies cosθ=(B−b)/(2b)=(√5−1)/4=cos72°.

problems.title: Two kinds of coins
problems.question: Gia has 28 coins, each worth 2 or 5 tetri, totaling 89 tetri. How many 2-tetri coins?
problems.idea: Use the total number and total value.

problems.title: Three consecutive trapezoid angles
problems.question: Three consecutive angles of a trapezoid are in ratio 3:2:1. Find its greatest angle.
problems.idea: One of the adjacent pairs must be supplementary.
formulas: Adjacent angles on either leg sum to 180°.
steps: Write the three angles 3t,2t,t. If 2t+t=180°, then 3t=180°, impossible.
Therefore 3t+2t=180°, giving t=36°. The fourth angle is 180°−36°=144°.

problems.title: A midpoint quadrilateral in a trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has obtuse angles 120°. The quadrilateral formed by the midpoints of its bases and diagonals has smaller diagonal 3.2. Find the leg.
problems.idea: Its diagonal lengths are the height and half the difference of the bases.
formulas: For leg l, h=l sin60°=√3l/2 and (B−b)/2=l cos60°=l/2.
steps: Place the trapezoid symmetrically: base midpoints lie on its axis, diagonal midpoints lie at mid-height.
The midpoint quadrilateral therefore has diagonals h and (B−b)/2. The smaller is l/2.

problems.title: Midpoints of two medians
problems.question: One triangle side has length b. Find the distance between the midpoints of the medians to the other two sides.
problems.idea: Write the two midpoint positions using vertex vectors.
formulas: For vertices A,B,C with BC=b,the midpoint of the median from B is M=A/4+B/2+C/4; the midpoint of the median from C is N=A/4+B/4+C/2.
steps: Subtract:N−M=(C−B)/4.
The distance is therefore one quarter of BC.

problems.title: Equal distances of two triangle centers from the base
problems.question: In an isosceles triangle, the incenter and circumcenter are equally distant from base AC. Which listed apex angle is possible?
problems.idea: Allow the circumcenter to lie below the base.
formulas: Set half-base=1, height=t, equal leg u=√(1+t²). Inradius=t/(u+1); circumcenter height=(t²−1)/(2t).
steps: For a 108° apex, t=cot54° and u=csc54°=√5−1.
Here t²=5−2√5, and (1−t²)(u+1)=2t², so the circumcenter height is the negative of the inradius.
Thus the distances agree. More generally the opposite-sign equation factors as u(u²+2u−4)=0, yielding u=√5−1 and apex 108°. The same-sign case gives the equilateral triangle.

problems.title: Recover a parallelogram perimeter from heights
problems.question: Heights from B to AD and CD are 3 cm and 4 cm. The acute angle is 30°. Find the perimeter.
problems.idea: Each height is a side times the sine of the included angle.
steps: The adjacent sides are 3/(1/2)=6 cm and 4/(1/2)=8 cm.
The perimeter is 2(6+8).

problems.title: Square a difference of three terms
problems.question: Given a²+b²+c²=30 and a−b−c=4, find bc−ac−ab.
problems.idea: The desired terms occur together when squaring.
steps: Subtract 30 and divide by 2.

problems.title: A rational expression on an interval
problems.question: If 4<a<5 and s=(4a−2)/(a−3), choose an interval containing s.
problems.idea: Separate a constant and a reciprocal.
steps: Adding 4 gives 9<s<14.

problems.title: The final digit of a power
problems.question: Find the last digit of 2018 raised to power 2019.
problems.idea: Only the last digit and the exponent modulo four matter.
formulas: Powers of 8 end 8,4,2,6 in a four-term cycle.
steps: 2019 leaves remainder 3 when divided by 4.
Use the third entry in the cycle.

problems.title: A right triangle constrained by its radii
problems.question: In a right triangle, the inradius plus circumradius equals one leg. Find the difference between its greatest and smallest angles.
problems.idea: Use the radius formulas for a right triangle.
steps: If this equals a, then b=a; similarly if it equals b.
The triangle is isosceles right, with angles 45°,45°,90°.
The requested difference is 90°−45°.

problems.title: Two angle bisectors meet an extended side
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD, bisectors at A,B meet line CD at M,N as drawn. AB=8 cm, BC=10 cm. Find MN.
problems.idea: The parallel sides create isosceles triangles.
steps: The bisector from A makes triangle ADM isosceles with AM meeting the extension beyond D, so DM=AD−DC=2.
Similarly BN meets beyond C and CN=2. Since CD=AB=8, MN=DM+DC+CN.

problems.title: Multiply powers of monomials
problems.question: Simplify $-[-1\frac12(-a^3)^4b^2]^3\cdot[-1\frac13a^4(-b)^5]^3$.
problems.idea: Simplify signs and powers inside each bracket first.
steps: The first bracket is −(3/2)a¹²b² and its cube is −(27/8)a³⁶b⁶.
The second is (4/3)a⁴b⁵ and its cube is (64/27)a¹²b¹⁵.
The leading minus changes their product to positive: (27/8)(64/27)a⁴⁸b²¹.

problems.title: Replace reciprocals with a sum and product
problems.question: Given x+y=xy/2 and 1/x−1/y=1/6, find x²+y².
problems.idea: Let s=x+y and p=xy.
steps: s²−s²/9=8s. Since xy≠0, s≠0, so s=9 and p=18.

problems.title: An equation with excluded denominators
problems.question: Solve x/(x+2)−(x−1)/(2x)=1/2.
problems.idea: Clear denominators after recording their restrictions.
steps: Expanding leaves −x+2=2x, so x=2/3. It is allowed.

problems.title: The least value for integer variables
problems.question: Integers a,b satisfy a>3 and b≤−4. Find the least possible 3a−4b.
problems.idea: Choose the smallest allowed a and largest allowed b.
steps: Thus 3a−4b≥28.
Equality occurs at a=4,b=−4.

problems.title: A raft time from a boat’s return trip
problems.question: A motorboat travels from A to B downstream in2 hours and returns upstream in4 hours. How long does a raft take from A to B?
problems.idea: A raft moves at the current speed; obtain that speed from the boat’s two speeds.
formulas: For distance d and boat/current speeds v,c:v+c=d/2,v−c=d/4.
steps: Subtract the speed equations:2c=d/2−d/4=d/4,so c=d/8.
A raft takes d/c=8 hours.

problems.title: A square with one side on the hypotenuse
problems.question: A square lies inside an isosceles right triangle, with two vertices on its legs and two on its hypotenuse. The hypotenuse is 2¼. Find the square perimeter.
problems.idea: Use similarity to the smaller triangle above the square.
formulas: For hypotenuse H, altitude to it is H/2. A parallel section at distance s has length H(1−2s/H)=H−2s.
steps: The square’s opposite side has length s, so s=H−2s.
Thus s=H/3=3/4 and the perimeter is 4s.

problems.title: Fruit-bearing trees cancel in a count
problems.question: An orchard contains only apple and pear trees. Fruit-bearing pear trees equal non-fruit-bearing apple trees. There are 25 apple trees. How many fruit-bearing trees in total?
problems.idea: Replace the pear count by the equal apple count.
steps: These two categories contain every apple tree once.
Their sum is 25.

problems.title: Find a coefficient ratio from two solutions
problems.question: (1,−1) and (−1,2) satisfy ax+by=c. Find (a+b)/c.
problems.idea: Substitute both ordered pairs.
steps: Equating gives 2a=3b. Set a=3t,b=2t,c=t.
For c≠0, (a+b)/c=5t/t.
problems.note: The ratio requires c≠0. If a=b=c=0 is allowed, the requested quotient is undefined; the usual intended assumption is a genuine line.

problems.title: A telescoping equation with unequal numerators
problems.question: Solve 1/[(x+1)(x+2)]+⋯+1/[(x+9)(x+10)]=10/[(x+1)(x+10)].
problems.idea: Rewrite each summand as a difference.
steps: Exclude x=−1,−2,…,−10. The sum telescopes to 1/(x+1)−1/(x+10)=9/[(x+1)(x+10)].
The equation would require 9=10 after multiplying by the nonzero denominator.

problems.title: Match numerators of identical rational expressions
problems.question: a/(x+1)+b/(x−1) is identical to (7x+10)/(x²−1). Find a²−b².
problems.idea: Combine the fractions and compare coefficients.
steps: a+b=7 and b−a=10.

problems.title: Complementary continued fractions
problems.question: Add the two printed nested fractions, whose outer forms are 1/[1+1/(1+t)] and 1/(2+t), with the same inner tail t.
problems.idea: Keep the shared tail as a single variable.
steps: Adding gives (1+t+1)/(2+t)=1 whenever the original fractions are defined.
There is no need to expand the inner tail involving n.

problems.title: Simplify two rational terms
problems.question: Simplify y²/(y−1)−(1−2y)/(1−y).
problems.idea: Reverse the sign of the second denominator.
steps: The expression is [y²+1−2y]/(y−1)=(y−1)²/(y−1).
Cancel one factor, retaining y≠1.

problems.title: An incenter in a semicircle
problems.question: AC is a diameter, B is on its semicircle, and K is the incenter of ABC. Find angle AKC.
problems.idea: The angle at the incenter depends on the third triangle angle.
formulas: B=90° by Thales’ theorem; angle AKC=90°+B/2.
steps: Substitute B=90° to get 90°+45°.
